screening.reason: Analyses raw ABIDE-I resting-state fMRI, builds functional connectivity networks via a uniform pipeline, and compares ASD vs TD graph Ricci curvature measures; satisfies inclusion 2-3.

evidence_spans.text: we apply Forman–Ricci and Ollivier–Ricci curvatures to compare  networks of ASD and typically developing individuals (N = 1112) from the Autism Brain Imaging  Data Exchange I (ABIDE-I) dataset.
evidence_spans.claim: Study compares ASD and TD networks from ABIDE-I (starting N=1112 before QC).

evidence_spans.text:
First, the subjects with missing anatomical or functional files were 
excluded. Second, all subjects from the imaging site Stanford were excluded as it is the only site with spiral image 
acquisition protocol. Third, all subjects from the imaging site Leuven-1 were excluded due to unknown repeti-
tion times for the functional scans.
evidence_spans.claim: Explicit site/QC exclusion rules: missing files, Stanford (spiral acquisition), Leuven-1 (unknown TR).

evidence_spans.text:
After removing subjects based on these exclusion criteria, we were left with 395 subjects in the ASD group and 
425 subjects in the TD group
evidence_spans.claim: Final analysed sample: 395 ASD and 425 TD (820 total).

evidence_spans.text: Subsequently, 200 regions of interest (ROIs)  or nodes were defined in the brain using the Schaefer atlas, and a 200 × 200 functional connectivity (FC) matrix  was generated for each subject by computing the Pearson correlation coefficient between the time-series of all  pairs of nodes.
evidence_spans.claim: Used the Schaefer 200-ROI atlas and Pearson correlation FC matrices.

evidence_spans.text: We used the CONN functional connectivity ­toolbox69 to process the rs- fMRI data from ABIDE-I.
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing pipeline was the CONN toolbox.

evidence_spans.text:
average edge FRC is significantly lower ( p < 0.05 , FDR-corrected) in the ASD group compared to the TD group 
in the graph density range 5–50%
evidence_spans.claim: Average edge Forman-Ricci curvature is significantly lower in ASD vs TD across most graph densities.

evidence_spans.text: We find brain-wide and region-specific ASD-related differences  for both Forman–Ricci and Ollivier–Ricci curvatures, with region-specific differences concentrated  in Default Mode, S
evidence_spans.claim: Region-specific ASD-related curvature differences concentrated in Default Mode and Somatomotor (and other) networks.

evidence_spans.text: Functional connectivity matrices and networks generated in our study, and all original codes are deposited  on GitHub and are publically available at https://​github.​com/​asama​llab/​Curva​ture-​FCN-​ASD as of the date of  publication.
evidence_spans.claim: FC matrices, networks and all analysis code were released on GitHub.

assessments.support: Explicit, multi-step QA/exclusion criteria (missing files, site-specific acquisition issues, PCP rater quality fail, QC-FC association checks) with resulting N by group.
Demographic/clinical Table 1 referenced; whole ABIDE-I (minus excluded sites) used.
CONN toolbox pipeline fully diagrammed (motion correction, slice-timing, outlier detection, segmentation/normalization, denoising, bandpass) with explicit QC-FC association checks.
Relies on ABIDE-I diagnostic labels; diagnostic instrument not restated in the sections read.
Motion covariates, outlier scans, and QC-FC distance-dependence explicitly checked and used as exclusion criteria; IQ deliberately not matched/excluded on, explained as a generalizability choice.
Linear regression to remove motion/WM/CSF confounds from BOLD signal; subjects with residual QC-FC correlation or distance-dependence excluded.
Standard Pearson correlation FC plus graph Ricci curvature (FRC/ORC) measures, computed across 49 graph densities for robustness.
Two-sample t-tests with FDR correction (alpha=0.05) applied for both brain-wide and node-level comparisons.

risk_of_bias.summary: Large, whole-ABIDE-I analysis with explicit, well-documented multi-step QC/exclusion criteria, a named preprocessing toolbox, FDR-corrected statistics, and full public release of FC matrices, networks and code.

charting.title: Graph Ricci curvatures reveal atypical functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder
charting.comorbidities_included_excluded: IQ was deliberately not used as an exclusion/matching criterion, to preserve generalizability to the typical ASD population
charting.new_dataset_contributed: no — releases derived FC matrices/networks and code, not new raw data
charting.dataset_openly_available: Yes — FC matrices, generated networks and all analysis code deposited on GitHub (https://github.com/asamallab/Curvature-FCN-ASD)
charting.specific_features: Pearson correlation FC among Schaefer 200-ROI atlas nodes; Forman-Ricci (FRC) and Ollivier-Ricci (ORC) edge/node curvatures computed across 49 graph densities (2-50%)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: CONN functional connectivity toolbox; Schaefer 200-parcel atlas; custom FRC/ORC code (NetworkX)
charting.importance_method: Node-level FRC/ORC and clustering-coefficient comparisons with FDR correction
charting.top_features_identified: Region-specific differences concentrated in Default Mode, Somatomotor and other resting-state networks (e.g. LH_SomMot_1, LH_SomMot_3, LH_Default_PFC_4)
charting.feature_change_direction: Lower average edge Forman-Ricci and Ollivier-Ricci curvature in ASD vs TD (both brain-wide and region-specific), concentrated in Default Mode and Somatomotor networks
charting.summary_key_findings: In 395 ASD and 425 TD individuals from ABIDE-I, average edge Forman-Ricci curvature was significantly lower in ASD than TD across most graph densities (5-50%, FDR-corrected), with a similar but less consistent pattern for Ollivier-Ricci curvature; region-specific curvature differences were concentrated in Default Mode, Somatomotor and other networks, and several node-level findings aligned with brain regions targeted by non-invasive brain stimulation (TMS/tDCS) studies in ASD.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Reduced Forman-Ricci and Ollivier-Ricci graph curvature in ASD, concentrated in Default Mode and Somatomotor networks

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE-I; n=395 ASD / 425 TD (820 total) after QC exclusions from an initial N=1112.
narrative_row.methods: CONN toolbox preprocessing; Schaefer 200-parcel atlas; Pearson FC; Forman-Ricci and Ollivier-Ricci graph curvature computed across 49 graph densities; two-sample t-tests with FDR correction.
narrative_row.outcomes: ASD showed significantly lower average edge Forman-Ricci curvature than TD across most graph densities, with a similar but less consistent Ollivier-Ricci pattern; region-specific differences concentrated in Default Mode and Somatomotor networks, overlapping with NIBS (TMS/tDCS) target regions in the literature.
narrative_row.key_limitations: IQ not matched/excluded on (a deliberate choice for generalizability); diagnostic instrument not restated; no formal multi-site harmonisation.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A fully reconstructible, whole-ABIDE-I graph-curvature analysis with public FC matrices, networks and code — a strong candidate for cross-study replication in the knowledge graph.
